artists.biography:
They Might Be Giants (sometimes abbreviated as TMBG) is an American alternative band formed in 1982 by John Flansburgh and John Linnell. During TMBG's early years Flansburgh and Linnell were frequently accompanied by a drum machine. In the early 1990s, TMBG became a full band. Currently, the members of TMBG are Flansburgh, Linnell, Marty Beller, Dan Miller, and Danny Weinkauf. They are best known for an unconventional and experimental style of alternative music. Over their career, the group has found success on the modern rock and CMJ charts. More recently they have found success in children's music, and in theme music for several television programs and films.
TMBG have released 15 studio albums. Flood has been certified platinum and their children's music album Here Come the ABCs has been certified gold. The band has won two Grammy Awards, one in 2002 for their song "Boss of Me", which served as the theme to Malcolm in the Middle. They won their second in 2009 for their album Here Come the 123s. The band has sold over 4 million records.

perplexity.description:
Glean is the seventeenth studio album by They Might Be Giants, released on April 21, 2015 on the band's Idlewild Recordings label. The album represents a significant moment in the band's career, as it compiles sixteen tracks drawn from the first four months of their revived 2015 Dial-A-Song project—a weekly song-and-video release series that harked back to the band's innovative 1983 answering machine service. Produced by longtime collaborator Pat Dillett, the album showcases the band's characteristic eclecticism across a diverse range of musical styles.

The album's sonic palette spans folk-pop sensibilities, manic violin-driven arrangements, and bluesy bass-heavy grooves, exemplified by tracks such as "Answer," "Music Jail, Pt. 1 & 2," and "Underwater Woman." This stylistic range reflects They Might Be Giants' commitment to uncompromising artistic variety, positioning Glean as vital work within their three-decade career. The album demonstrates the band's continued ability to balance accessibility with experimental impulses, maintaining the inventive spirit that has defined their approach to alternative rock.

Glean arrived following the 2013 album Nanobots and was well-received by the band's fanbase, with the Dial-A-Song project itself generating widespread enthusiasm among both longtime supporters and new listeners. The album's release across multiple formats—CD, vinyl, and digital—reflected the band's ongoing embrace of technological innovation in music distribution, a hallmark of their career trajectory from pioneering downloadable albums to contemporary streaming platforms.
